correctness.rationale: Every similar complex 2-by-2 pair is scalar, nontrivial Jordan, or simple spectrum. The unique nontrivial polynomial invariant in the latter two types is a square-zero part or a spectral involution, whose norms are preserved under tensoring with any nonzero Hilbert identity. Conjugation by any (possibly entangled) amplified similarity bounds their norm ratio below by its condition number. Orthonormal canonical forms give an explicit diagonal planar intertwiner of exactly that condition number. The extremal pair of involutions attains \(\theta_{2,q}(t)=t\) for every positive integer multiplicity and every \(t\geq1\), including the endpoint. The exact rational/complex numeric checker passed 2992 assertions, supporting but not replacing the proof.

value.rationale: Jiang et al. introduced the similarity envelope in 2026 and raised the possibility of exact condition-number cancellation. Aouichaoui showed that the equality fails in some larger dimensions, heightening the question of an exact first-dimensional boundary. A complete, attained classification in base dimension two (all Jordan types and all nonzero Hilbert multiplicities) resolves that natural remaining boundary and quantifies its sharp envelope, rather than computing an arbitrary isolated example.
